sections.h2: How a West Palm Beach owner can close quickly
sections.html:
The quickest paths are a sale to a cash buyer or investor and a listing priced to move. If timing is what you need most, balance three things: the price, the number of days to close, and how many repairs the buyer will insist on.

  • Cash or investor sale: no repairs asked of you, and the closing date is frequently yours to set.
  • Agent listing: more potential buyers and often more money, but showings and loan approval take time.
  • Hybrid: put it on the market, and switch to a cash offer if interest stays thin.

Put three questions to every buyer: how title problems get handled, who orders the title search, and what happens to the deposit if they back out. With so many houses dating from earlier decades, those answers count as much as the price. Then add up what each offer leaves you after deed tax, title charges, unpaid taxes and any rental license filing. A big headline number sometimes nets less than a modest cash bid.

West Palm Beach is the seat of Palm Beach County and was incorporated on November 5, 1894. Buyers know The Square, Clematis Street, Antique Row and Northwood Village, and the Grassy Waters Everglades Preserve sits on the western edge.

Housing here spans many eras, with historic neighborhoods next to newer waterfront and downtown buildings. Older houses often come with deferred maintenance, and an as-is sale means you never pay for those repairs before listing.

Every rental unit in the city needs a rental tax application, whether it is a short-term listing on a platform like Airbnb or a lease to a tenant. Processing generally takes seven to 10 business days.

Owners also complete a zoning review that verifies the number of units. Inspectors check interior and exterior conditions such as working appliances, window screens, paved parking and visible address numbers. After applying, the owner contacts Code Enforcement at (561) 822-1465.

West Palm Beach rental property types
TypeDescriptionExtra requirement
Type 1Owner-occupied single-family, multifamily or duplexProof the property is owner-occupied; owner name must match the recorded deed
Type 2Not owner-occupied single-family or duplexEntire dwelling unit rented
Type 3Not owner-occupied multifamily, such as apartments or condosBuilding and unit counts; compliance with any geographic caps

When you sell a rental, tell the buyer which type it is. Ownership on the application must match the deed recorded with the Palm Beach County Clerk's Office, which means the new owner files separately.

Open violations and unpermitted additions can slow a closing. An extra unit added without paperwork is a likely sticking point, since rental owners must hold a license and pass an inspection.

The code compliance division sets minimum standards for substandard housing conditions, trash and debris, yard upkeep and parking areas.

Walk your lot before listing and look for visible problems, and confirm that any garage conversion or added unit has permits on file. Call Code Enforcement to ask whether your address has open cases. Cash buyers will take a property with problems, but they subtract the cleanup from their price.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and discounts
sections.html:
The county sends out over 600,000 property tax bills by November 1, and they can be paid from that day through March 31. In August the Property Appraiser mails a proposed-tax notice.

  • November: 4 percent discount
  • December: 3 percent discount
  • January: 2 percent discount
  • February: 1 percent discount
  • March: no discount; April 1: taxes become delinquent

Once a tax is delinquent, you cannot pay it online, and a postmark no longer proves timely payment. If a bill reaches you after you sold, pass it to the new owner or notify the office with a Property Sold Form. Call the Property Appraiser at (561) 355-2866 about mailing addresses or exemptions, and the Tax Collector at (561) 355-2264 about delinquent amounts.

Your bill includes non-ad valorem charges as well as ad valorem tax. The Solid Waste Authority fee is one example, set by the type of property.

Certain owners can put off payment. A homestead deferral request goes to the tax collector on Form DR-570 by March 31, and installment plan applications follow by May 1.

Non-homestead property has its own protection: assessed value growth is limited to 10 percent each year. Homestead property gets the Save Our Homes cap: yearly increases cannot exceed the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. That cap resets when title changes, so your buyer may be assessed higher than you were come the next January 1.

If you are moving to another Florida home, part of that savings can travel with you. Portability allows three years, counted from the January 1 after you give up the old homestead, and Form DR-501T is filed with the DR-501 by March 1.

The state taxes deeds at $0.70 for each $100 of price, and Palm Beach County pays that standard rate. All parties to the deed are liable, while your contract settles who actually pays.

Recording with the clerk costs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each later one. Add a trust fund charge of $1.00 on the first page and $0.50 on later pages, and a $4 per page technology charge. Ask for the full settlement statement before signing so you see every line.

sections.h2: Papers to gather before you list
sections.html:
A tidy folder speeds up every offer. Start with your recorded deed, which shows the exact owner name the city and county will see. Add your latest tax bill, a mortgage payoff letter if you owe a lender, and any permit records for additions or major repairs.

For a rental, include the current rental tax application and the lease. For an older house, include dated receipts for the roof, air conditioning and plumbing. A buyer who can see this record spends less time guessing, and fewer guesses mean fewer price cuts late in the deal.

Without a mortgage, a cash deal has no lender appraisal and no underwriting wait. On an older house that matters, because an appraiser's repair list can derail a financed purchase. You also avoid staging and weeks of showings.

Once you accept an offer, a title search comes first, then a look at the settlement statement, then you sign the deed and the clerk records it. If tenants occupy the house, write into the contract whether they stay and who handles the rental license afterward. Also ask the buyer how soon funds will reach you after recording, since that timing varies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental property in West Palm Beach without ending the rental license?
faqs.a: The buyer should apply separately. Because the license application follows the owner on the recorded deed, a new owner files in their own name. Ask the Development Services business tax staff how to close your account.

faqs.q: How long does the West Palm Beach rental license take?
faqs.a: The city says it is generally processed in seven to 10 business days. A zoning review of the unit count is part of the process.

faqs.q: When do West Palm Beach property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. From then on, you cannot pay online, and a postmark stops counting as proof of payment.

faqs.q: Which discount applies if I pay in December?
faqs.a: December payments earn 3 percent off. The other months run 4 percent in November, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: Must I pull a permit for repairs I make before selling?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Florida's 2026 exemption for projects under $7,500 has limits, and electrical, plumbing and structural jobs still require permits. Check with the city's Development Services staff first.
